correctness.rationale: PASS: Normalize the base triangle by an invertible affine map. Independent uniform arclength fractions stay iid uniform on (0,1), and area fraction is invariant. Direct affine-cevian algebra gives Z=T^2/Q with T=H(w-w0), H=uv+(1-u)(1-v)>0, w0=(1-u)(1-v)/H, and positive Q=(1-u+uv)(1-w+uw)(1-v+vw)<=1. Therefore a one-dimensional sqrt-epsilon tube around the Ceva surface contributes 2 sqrt(Q0)/H for each (u,v); the global bound 2/H is integrable (linear corner singularities only) and proves dominated-convergence asymptotic. Barycentric coordinates of the first intersection P obey u=b/(b+c),v=c/(a+c). The measured Jacobian from a,b to auxiliary triangle angles was independently finite-differenced at three generic/equilateral points and equals A′B′C′/2, giving sqrt(Q0)/H du dv=(sin alpha+sin beta+sin gamma)/8 d alpha d beta. Integration yields 3pi/8 and thus 3pi/4 sqrt-epsilon. On compact parameter sets the signed normalized defect s=sgn(T)sqrt(Z/epsilon) changes coordinates smoothly with locally uniformly convergent densities; dominance controls boundary tails, proving joint L1/total-variation convergence. Resulting angular density is (sin alpha+sin beta+sin(alpha+beta))/(6pi) on angular simplex times s in (-1,1), and acute auxiliary probability 1/pi. Independent 300k-sample Monte Carlo ratios at epsilon .02/.005/.001 were 2.140/2.250/2.314 approaching 3pi/4=2.356; those finite experiments do not prove the asymptotic.

Unindexed older probability papers remain a genuine historical uncertainty.
